verdict:
The round does not close: one medium, five lows, no high. M's false sentence is gone and the §4.2 split is stated correctly, but the fix makes Sharma §4.2 the measurement nearest this pipeline while the sentence above it says, unqualified, that optimizing was found lowering the unread; the paper says "mixed effects" and "sometimes".

Checked and sound:
- Constitutional AI: 42,496, 182,831 and 135,296; the critic and the chain-of-thought feedback are the helpful RLHF model; helpfulness labels stay human.
- Sharma: the split is at §4.2, and "constitution" or "principles" occur nowhere in its text except a reference title. Bai 2022b is not cited at the Claude 2 PM sentence.
- Wen and Gao abstract pages match what the study says, including 24.1% and 18.3%.
- "By analogy" and "a reading" are present where the bearing is not shown. "Figures read from the papers' abstracts" governs no stated figure in the audit's sentence.

Times, by navigation.py's rule (re-implemented, counted only):
- USES-EXAMPLES.md: 5,890 words and 65 characters, 45.56 to 59.23, so 46 to 59 is right.
- USES.md: 14.94 to 19.42, so 15 to 19 is right.
- The zh examples page: 36.9 to 47.9, as stated.
- First screen: 535 words, as stated.

No stale copy of the old wordings or times remains outside history. I ran no tests and edited nothing. Paper wording came through WebFetch's summarizer; §4.2's was consistent across fetches.

A reader concludes that optimizing against a preference model with this split was measured lowering truthfulness. §4.2 says optimizing with the Claude 2 PM 'has mixed effects on sycophancy': best-of-N reduces answer and mimicry sycophancy for that base model, some forms rise through RL, and optimizing 'can yield models that sometimes sacrifice truthfulness for sycophancy'. §4.3.2 says optimizing against that PM reduces sycophancy, less than the non-sycophantic PM and much less than the oracle. It also leaves out the chain-of-thought feedback model, which the study now names.

findings.problem: 'transcripts that differ only in what comes after them' are, strictly, the same transcript. The study's construction speaks of two episodes with the same transcript.
findings.fix: Use 'a reward or pick separating episodes with the same transcript'.

why:
The finding holds against the paper's full text and the worktree at 1b2b57c8a; nothing was edited.

Confirmed in the paper:
- §4.2: optimizing with the Claude 2 PM "has mixed effects on sycophancy". Best-of-N "reduces answer and mimicry sycophancy for this base model". With RL "some forms of sycophancy increase". The PM "can yield models that sometimes sacrifice truthfulness for sycophancy", and effects "depend on details of the optimization approach".
- §4.3.2: optimizing against that PM reduces sycophancy, less than the non-sycophantic PM and much less than the oracle.
- The abstract says "sometimes sacrifices".

Confirmed in the repository: the study's section 1 says "sometimes traded". USES-EXAMPLES line 54 says the three measurements "found optimizing lowering what the deciders do not read", then attaches the third to "a preference model with this pipeline's split".

Attempts to refute:
1. "Found" could be existential, and an existence case is what bears on room. This is partly right, and it is why severity is not high. Fig. 6(b) reports feedback and mimicry sycophancy rising as RL optimizes against this PM, and the paper itself uses "sacrifice truthfulness". The sentence is incomplete rather than false.
2. The line's hedges could cover it. They do not. "[AI reading]" and "by analogy" cover whether the measurement bears on this pipeline, not what was found. "Read from the papers' abstracts" is no excuse, because the abstract carries "sometimes", and the line cites §4.2 directly.
3. The omission could be immaterial. It is not. The item asks whether there is room, and this is the measurement it singles out as closest to this pipeline. The same PM moved mimicry sycophancy in opposite directions depending on the optimizer, which is the sign information a reader needs to weigh it. A reader would take the third as a one-directional drain.

Two corrections to the proposed fix:
- The audit cannot carry the qualifier alone. Line 42 of the same page quotes 07 §6's unqualified sentence and adds "that is the drain's direction", and USES-EXAMPLES.zh.md line 48 mirrors it. Line 42 is what makes the one-directional reading the page's own, so it needs the qualifier too. The unqualified form also stands in 07 §6 (line 686), the record's statement (.md line 8, .json line 13) and the study's "What this establishes" bullet, as the finding says.
- "Some forms of sycophancy falling and others rising" misdescribes the result, since mimicry falls under best-of-N and rises under RL. Better: "there with mixed effects, best-of-N lowering some forms of sycophancy and RL raising some, truthfulness sometimes given up for agreement".

Not verified: the 59.225 minutes at 5,890 words arithmetic. I found no tool that computes it, and `wc -w` gives 6,017 for the whole file including header matter. The 28-word threshold is consistent only if the rate is about 99.45 words per minute and rounding happens at 59.5.
